name: book-pocket
title: Book Pocket
description: Book covers tucked in a frosted acrylic pocket: they drop in, and rise and fan out while pressed or hovered.

perf.budget: Covers move by transforms from one UI-thread spring; the pocket is one blur view over them. Nothing animates at rest.

measurements.notes: Measured with four pockets, each a blur view over its covers. Frame stats put app work at about 2 ms and render-thread work at 7 ms a frame; the rest is the emulator waiting on its virtual GPU.

a11y.reducedMotion: Covers appear in place and jump between tucked and lifted without the spring.
a11y.screenReader: The pocket reads as one button with the shelf and count ("Fantasy, 8 books").
a11y.touchTarget: The whole pocket and its covers are the button.

meta.guide:
## Usage

```tsx
import { BookPocket } from '@/components/kinetik/book-pocket';

<BookPocket
  title="Fantasy"
  count={8}
  books={shelf.slice(0, 3).map((b) => ({ id: b.id, title: b.title, cover: { uri: b.coverUrl } }))}
  onPress={() => router.push('/shelf/fantasy')}
/>;
```

## When to use

- Grouping a collection (books, albums, decks) into tappable shelves where the covers do the talking.

## When not to use

- Long lists of single items: use a list or a grid of covers.

## Notes

- Up to four covers show, back to front. Pass `cover` for an image; without one a typographic cover is drawn from `tones`.
- Covers rise while the pocket is pressed (and while a pointer hovers on the web), then slide back on release.
- The pocket blurs only the covers behind it (`BlurTargetView`), so it works the same on Android, iOS and the web.

docs: Prefer `npx kinetik-ui add book-pocket`: it installs dependencies with expo install, so versions match your Expo SDK.
